body.translated_text:
(Vaidya 174)
<s>Nairātmyaparipṛcchā nāma Mahāyānasūtram</s> (The Mahāyāna Sūtra Called "The Inquiry Concerning Non-Self")

body.text: atha te tīrthikā upalambhadṛṣṭayaḥ savikalpāḥ savitarkā mahāyānikamupasṛtya sādarakṛtāñjalipuṭā nairātmyapraśnaṃ paripṛcchanti sma - nairātmakaṃ śarīramiti kulaputra sarvajñena nirdiśyate | yadi śarīraṃ nairātmakam, paramātmā na vidyate | tat kasmātsakāśādete hasitaruditakrīḍitakrodhamānerṣyāṃpaiśunyādayaḥ samutpadyante? tadasmākaṃ saṃdehaṃ mocayitumarhati bhagavān - kimasti śarīre paramātmā, kiṃ vā nāsti?
body.translated_text: Then those non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthikas</s>), holding views of apprehension, with conceptual elaboration and discursive thought, approached the <s>Mahāyānist</s> and, with palms reverently joined, asked a question concerning non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>): 'The body is without self (<s>nairātmaka</s>)—thus, O son of good family, the Omniscient One declares. If the body is without self, the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) does not exist. Then from what cause do these [phenomena]—laughter, weeping, play, anger, pride, envy, slander, and the rest—arise? May the Blessed One deign to resolve our doubt: does a supreme self exist in the body, or does it not?'

body.text: mahāyānikāḥ prāhuḥ - mārṣāḥ, śarīre paramātmā astītyucyate, na hi nāstīti | dvayamatra nocyate | asti paramātmetyucyamāne mārṣā mithyāpralāpaḥ | yadyasti, tatkathaṃ mārṣāḥ keśanakhadantacarmaromasirāmāṃsāsthimedamajjāsnāyuplīhāntranālaśiraḥkaracaraṇāṅgasakalaśarīre sa bāhyābhyantare vicāryamāṇe na dṛśyate paramātmā?
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'Sirs, it is said that a supreme self exists in the body, but it is not said that it does not exist. Neither of these two is stated. If one says "a supreme self exists," sirs, that is false prattle. If it exists, then why, sirs—when one searches throughout hair, nails, teeth, skin, body-hair, veins, flesh, bones, marrow, fat, sinews, spleen, intestines, tubes, head, hands, feet, limbs, and the entire body, both external and internal—is the supreme self not seen?'

body.text: tīrthikāḥ prāhuḥ - na dṛśyate kulaputra paramātmā | māṃsacakṣuṣā vayaṃ na paśyāmaḥ | kadāciddivyacakṣuṣaḥ paśyanti |
body.translated_text: The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'The supreme self is not seen, O son of good family. We do not see [it] with the fleshly eye. Perhaps those with the divine eye see [it].'

body.text: mahāyānikāḥ prāhuḥ - na mārṣā divyacakṣuṣo 'pi paśyanti | yasya na varṇo na rūpaṃ na saṃskāraḥ, tatkathaṃ dṛśyate?
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'No, sirs, those with the divine eye do not see [it] either. That which has no color, no form, no conditioned characteristics—how could it be seen?'
The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'Does it not exist then?'

body.text: mahāyānikāḥ prāhuḥ - nāstītyucyamāne mārṣā mithyāpralāpaḥ | yadi nāsti, tatkathamasya ete hasitaruditakrīḍitakrodhamānerṣyāpaiśunyādayaḥ saṃbhavanti? tena nāstīti vaktuṃ na pāryate | ubhāvetau dvau nocyete |
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'If one says "it does not exist," sirs, that too is false prattle. If it does not exist, then how do these [phenomena]—laughter, weeping, play, anger, pride, envy, slander, and the rest—occur in it? Therefore, it cannot be said that it does not exist. Neither of these two is stated.'

body.text: tīrthikāḥ prāhuḥ - yadi kulaputra nocyate astīti vā nāstīti vā, tatkimatrālambanaṃ bhavatu?
body.translated_text: The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'If, O son of good family, it is not said either that it exists or that it does not exist, then what is the support (<s>ālambana</s>) here?'

body.text: mahāyānikāḥ prāhuḥ - na mārṣāḥ kiṃcidālambanaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'Sirs, there is no support whatsoever.'
The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'Is it empty, like space?'
The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'So it is, sirs, so it is. Empty, like space.'

body.text: tīrthikāḥ prāhuḥ - yadyevaṃ kulaputra, tadete hasitaruditakrīḍitakrodhamānerṣyāpaiśunyādayaḥ kathaṃ draṣṭavyāḥ?
body.translated_text: The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'If so, O son of good family, then how are these [phenomena]—laughter, weeping, play, anger, pride, envy, slander, and the rest—to be regarded?'
The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'They should be regarded as like a dream, an illusion, and a magical display (<s>indrajāla</s>).'

body.text: tīrthikāḥ prāhuḥ - kīdṛśī maya, kīdṛśaḥ svapnaḥ, kidṛśa indrajāla iti?
body.translated_text: The <s>tīrthikas</s> replied: 'What is illusion (<s>māyā</s>) like? What is a dream like? What is a magical display (<s>indrajāla</s>) like?'

body.text: mahāyānikāḥ prāhuḥ - upalakṣaṇamātraṃ mayā agrāhā, pratibhāsamātraṃ svapnaḥ prakṛtiśūnyatāsvarūpaḥ, indrajālaḥ kṛtrimaprayogaḥ | evaṃ mārṣāḥ sarve svapnamāyendrajālasadṛśā draṣṭavyāḥ | punaraparaṃ dvau bhedau vinirdiṣṭau yaduta saṃvṛtiḥ paramārthaśca | tatra saṃvṛtirnāma ayamātmā, ayaṃ (#Nparipṛ, Vaidya 175#) paraḥ | evaṃ jīvaḥ puruṣaḥ pudgalaḥ kārakaḥ vedakaḥ | dhanaputrakalatrādikalpanā yā, sā saṃvṛtirnāma | yatra nātmā na paraḥ, evaṃ na jīvo na pudgalaḥ na puruṣaḥ na kārakaḥ na vedakaḥ na dhanaṃ - - - - - sā madhyamā pratipattirdharmāṇām | tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyānists</s> replied: 'Illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is merely a semblance, ungraspable; a dream is merely an appearance, empty by nature in its essential form; a magical display (<s>indrajāla</s>) is an artificial contrivance. Thus, sirs, all [phenomena] should be regarded as like a dream, an illusion, and a magical display. Furthermore, two divisions are taught, namely the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). Therein, the conventional is: "this is self, this is other"—thus <s>jīva</s> (life-force), <s>puruṣa</s> (person), <s>pudgala</s> (individual), agent, experiencer, the conceptual construction of wealth, sons, wife, and so forth—that is called the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). Where there is neither self nor other, likewise neither <s>jīva</s> nor <s>pudgala</s> nor <s>puruṣa</s> nor agent nor experiencer nor wealth... that is the middle understanding (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. Regarding this, it is said:'

children.translated_text: The conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>)—two divisions have been illuminated.
The conventional is a worldly <s>dharma</s>; the ultimate is supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>). // 1 //
Beings who have fallen into conventional <s>dharma</s>, following the power of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>),
wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) for a long time, not knowing the ultimate truth. // 2 //
The conventional is a worldly <s>dharma</s>; the unwise construct it.
Through false conceptual construction (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>), they experience sufferings. // 3 //

children.text: muktimārgaṃ na paśyanti andhā bālāḥ pṛthagjanāḥ |
children.translated_text: They do not see the path to liberation—blind, childish, ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>);
they arise and cease unceasingly in the five destinies (<s>gati</s>). // 4 //
Deluded, they wander like a wheel, enveloped by worldly <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: paramārthaṃ na jānanti bhavo yatra nirudhyate |
children.translated_text: they do not know the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) where becoming (<s>bhava</s>) ceases.
Enmeshed in the net of existence (<s>bhava</s>), they transmigrate again and again. // 5 //
Just as the moon and the sun come and go,

children.text: bhavaṃ cyutiṃ tathā loke punarāyānti yānti ca || 6 ||
children.translated_text: so too in the world, beings come and go [through] birth (<s>bhava</s>) and death (<s>cyuti</s>). // 6 //
All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are impermanent, unstable, momentarily perishing;
Therefore, the knower of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) should abandon the domain of conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>).
The gods who dwell in heavenly realms — <s>gandharva</s>s, <s>apsaras</s>es, and the like —

children.text: cyutirasti ca sarveṣāṃ tatsarvaṃ saṃvṛteḥ phalam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: there is falling away for all of them; all that is the fruit of conventional [truth].
<s>Siddha</s>s (perfected beings), <s>vidyādhara</s>s (knowledge-bearers), <s>yakṣa</s>s (nature spirits), <s>kinnara</s>s (celestial musicians), and great serpents (<s>mahoraga</s>s) —

children.text: punaste narakaṃ yānti tatsarvaṃ saṃvṛteḥ phalam || 9 ||
children.translated_text: they again go to hell; all that is the fruit of conventional [truth].
Having attained the status of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), universal sovereignty, and the highest station,
there is rebirth in an animal womb; all that is the fruit of conventional [truth].
Therefore, having abandoned all this — the divine, heavenly, great bliss —
the wise one should constantly cultivate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), which is luminous.
Without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), without support, entirely empty (<s>sarvaśūnya</s>), without abode,
transcending all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>) — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

children.text: na kāṭhinyaṃ na ca mṛdutvaṃ na coṣṇaṃ naiva śītalam |
children.translated_text: Neither hard nor soft, neither hot nor cold,

children.text: na saṃsparśaṃ na ca grāhyaṃ bodhicittasya lakṣaṇam || 13 ||
children.translated_text: neither tangible nor graspable — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

children.text: na dīrghaṃ nāpi vā hrasvaṃ na piṇḍaṃ na trikoṇakam |
children.translated_text: Neither long nor short, neither round nor triangular,

children.text: na kṛśaṃ nāpi na sthūlaṃ bodhicittasya lakṣaṇam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: neither thin nor thick — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

children.text: na śveta nāpi raktaṃ ca na kṛṣṇaṃ na ca pītakam |
children.translated_text: Neither white nor red, neither black nor yellow,
without color and without form — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.
Without modification, without appearance, without growth, without binding,
formless, resembling space — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.
Transcending [all] meditation, beyond the reach of <s>tīrthika</s>s (non-Buddhist teachers),
having the form of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom) — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.
Incomparable, without appearance, invisible, and utterly peaceful,
pure by nature, without substance — such is the characteristic of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca tena sādṛśyaṃ niḥsāraṃ budbudopamam |
children.translated_text: And everything is similar to that — without essence, like a bubble,
impermanent, selfless (<s>nairātmya</s>), resembling an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) and a mirage (<s>marīci</s>).
Like a lump of clay that has become a pot, filled with manifold conceptual elaboration,
conjoined with attachment, aversion, and the like — merely a dream and an illusion.

children.text: abhrāntare yathā vidyut kṣaṇādapi na dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: Just as lightning within a cloud is not seen even for an instant,
so through the vision of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom), one should cultivate the supreme state.

children.text: krīḍitaṃ hasitaṃ nityaṃ jalpitaṃ ruditaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Playing, laughing, constant chattering, weeping,

children.text: nṛtyaṃ gītaṃ tathā vādyaṃ sarvaṃ svapnopamaṃ hi tat || 22 ||
children.translated_text: dancing, singing, and music — all that is indeed like a dream.
All the formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of all embodied beings are like an illusion and a dream;

children.text: svapnaṃ ca cittasaṃkalpaṃ cittaṃ ca gaganopamam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: dreams are mental constructions (<s>citta-saṃkalpa</s>), and the mind itself is like space.
One who constantly cultivates this approach of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom),

children.text: sa sa rvapāpanirmuktaḥ prāpnoti paramaṃ padam || 24 ||
children.translated_text: freed from all sins, attains the supreme state.
This is the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), illuminated by all the <s>Buddha</s>s.
Having cultivated this meditation here, one obtains the auspicious <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
As many as are the faults of conventional [truth], so many are the virtues of cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>);
cessation is non-arising — it is not stained by any faults.

body.text: atha te tīrthikāstuṣṭā vikalparahitāstadā bhāvanāṃ samādhāya mahāyānayajñalābhino 'bhūvanniti ||
body.translated_text: Then those <s>tīrthika</s>s (non-Buddhist teachers), satisfied and free from conceptual construction, having established [themselves in] meditation, became recipients of the offering of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
Thus ends the <s>Nairātmyaparipṛcchā</s> (The Questions on Selflessness) in the exposition of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
